questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Explain the functions of the following devices in computer network:

(i) Modem

(ii) Repeater

(iii) Router (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Functions of the devices (6 marks, 2 marks each)**

- **(i) Modem** (modulator-demodulator): it converts the digital signals of the computer into analogue signals that can travel on a telephone line or other analogue medium (modulation), and converts the incoming analogue signals back to digital signals (demodulation). It connects the computer or the network to the Internet service provider.
- **(ii) Repeater:** it receives a weak signal, regenerates (amplifies and cleans) it and sends it on, so that the signal can travel over a longer distance than the maximum length of the cable, and extends the network.
- **(iii) Router:** it connects two or more different networks (for example a local network and the Internet) and forwards data packets from one network to another, using the IP addresses and choosing the best path for each packet.

**Types of network (6 marks, 2 marks each)**

- **(i) A college computer room:** a **LAN (Local Area Network)**: the computers are in one room, so they are linked over a very short distance, with cables or Wi-Fi, and share printers, files and an Internet connection.
- **(ii) A hospital:** a **LAN (Local Area Network)**: the wards, offices and laboratories are in one building or compound, and the computers share patient records and equipment. (If the hospital had branches in several towns, those sites would be linked as a WAN.)
- **(iii) The city of Yaounde:** a **MAN (Metropolitan Area Network)**: it covers a whole city, a larger area than a LAN but smaller than a country or the world.

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Justify your answers in (b) above. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Justification (3 marks, 1 mark each)**

- A college computer room and a hospital each occupy a **small geographical area** (one room, or one building or compound), so a LAN is enough: it is fast, cheap to install and easy to manage and to secure.
- A city such as Yaounde spreads over **tens of kilometres**, which is too large for a LAN and too small to need a WAN, so a MAN, which links many buildings and LANs of the same city with high-capacity links (fibre optic, wireless), is the suitable type.
- A network is classified by the **distance it covers**: LAN (one room or building), MAN (a city), WAN (countries and continents).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) Figure 1 shows a file path.

`C : CSC / Unit1 / John.docx`

with the labels A under `C :`, B under `CSC`, C under `John` and D under `.docx`.

**Figure 1**

(i) Name the sections of the file path labelled A, B, C, D. (4 marks)

(ii) Give the significance of the part labelled D. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Sections of the file path (4 marks, 1 mark each)**

| Label | Part | Name of the section |
|---|---|---|
| A | `C:` | the drive (the storage device, here the hard disk drive C) |
| B | `CSC` | a folder (directory) on that drive (it contains the sub-folder `Unit1`) |
| C | `John` | the file name |
| D | `.docx` | the file extension |

**(ii) Significance of D (1 mark)**

The extension `.docx` shows the **type (format) of the file**: it is a word-processing document (Microsoft Word). The operating system uses it to know which application program must be used to open the file.
